Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: Can MVFA's segmentation adapters learn transferable localisation from image-level labels alone? Today they learn only from pixel masks of BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC. We replace the Dice and Focal seg_loss with a multiple-instance objective applied at all four levels to the segmentation-branch patch-to-text similarity map (mean of the top 2% patch anomaly probabilities; max and mean pooling as ablations), and train on all five source datasets with masks discarded. Primary question and hypothesis: because every patch is scored against a shared text anchor, image-level supervision aligns patch-level evidence with the text 'abnormal' direction, so the learned localisation transfers to the unseen modality and retains at least 80% of mask-supervised MVFA's pixel-level AUROC (with PRO and image AUROC also reported). A visual-only MIL control (same operator on a linear patch classifier without text anchors) tests whether text anchoring is responsible. Secondary analyses: per-level localisation quality, and a label-budget comparison on two held-out modalities between image-labelled training and mask-supervised training on 10%, 30% and 100% of the masked images.

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Normal-bank pseudo-masks: localising anomalies in image-labelled source data by distance to that dataset's normal patches
SUMMARY: Use the image labels of each source dataset to build a memory bank of its normal patches, mark patches of its abnormal images that are far from every normal patch as pseudo-anomalous, and train MVFA's segmentation adapters with Dice and Focal on these pseudo-masks.
HYPOTHESIS: Pseudo-masks from k-nearest-neighbour distance to a source dataset's own normal-patch bank reach at least 0.4 pixel-level IoU with true masks on BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC training images, and segmentation adapters trained on them for all five source datasets retain at least 80% of mask-supervised MVFA's zero-shot pixel-AUROC margin over chance on the held-out modality.
RATIONALE: Parent 1 creates pseudo-masks from the detection branch, which reviewers doubted localises well because it is mean-pooled; parent 2 sharpens the text reference. A different source of localisation is already implicit in image labels: within one dataset, the normal images define what normal tissue looks like, so an abnormal image's patches that have no close normal neighbour are anomalous. This is MVFA's own few-shot memory-bank principle (1 - max cosine to normal patches), applied offline to the source data at scale to manufacture dense supervision for the segmentation branch.
METHOD: 1) New script make_bank_masks.py: for each source dataset, extract frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 patch tokens at the four MVFA levels for all normal training images (coreset-subsample to 10% with greedy k-center, as in PatchCore); for each abnormal training image compute per-patch score = mean over levels of (1 - max cosine to the bank); pseudo-mask = patches above the 99th percentile of the same score on held-out normal images of that dataset, restricted to the foreground (Otsu), upsampled to 240x240. 2) train_zero.py: segmentation loss = Focal + Dice on pseudo-masks for every source image (normal images: empty mask); true masks are never loaded. 3) Hyper-parameters as MVFA (lr 1e-4, 50 epochs, batch size 1); coreset ratio and percentile as ablations.
EXPERIMENT: BMAD zero-shot leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); no source masks used by the proposed variants; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as reference; 3 seeds; pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Baselines: mask-supervised MVFA; detection-to-segmentation pseudo-masks; asymmetric SigLIP-MIL. Ablations: bank features (frozen CLIP vs. adapted), percentile (97/99/99.5), coreset ratio. Metrics: pseudo-mask IoU and precision (analysis only, on datasets with masks), held-out pixel AUROC, PRO, image AUROC. Falsification: pseudo-mask IoU below 0.25 or retention below 60%.

Idea B:
TITLE: Change detection against a retrieved normal twin: optimal-transport pseudo-masks from image labels
SUMMARY: For each abnormal source image, retrieve its most similar normal image from the same dataset, align their patch tokens with entropic optimal transport, and treat the patch mass of the abnormal image that cannot be transported cheaply as the pseudo-mask for MVFA's segmentation adapters.
HYPOTHESIS: Unbalanced-OT residual mass against a retrieved normal twin yields pseudo-masks with at least 0.05 higher IoU than counterfactual-replacement masks on BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC training images, and segmentation adapters trained on them retain at least 80% of mask-supervised MVFA's held-out pixel-AUROC margin over chance.
RATIONALE: By analogy with change detection in remote sensing, where a before/after pair reveals what changed, an abnormal image paired with an anatomically similar normal image reveals the lesion as the part that has no counterpart. Image labels provide the normal pool; global CLIP features retrieve the twin; unbalanced optimal transport handles small misalignments and lets lesion patches remain unmatched instead of being forced onto normal tissue. Unlike counterfactual replacement, this does not depend on the detection branch's mean-pooled score being sensitive to single patches.
METHOD: 1) Twin retrieval: frozen CLIP CLS cosine within the same source dataset's normal training images (top-1, or average over top-3). 2) Patch tokens at levels 2-3 (mid-level, more spatial); cost C_ij = 1 - cos; unbalanced Sinkhorn (POT library, epsilon 0.05, marginal relaxation 0.5). 3) Residual mass per abnormal patch = 1 - transported mass; pseudo-mask = patches above the 95th percentile of residual on normal-normal pairs from the same dataset. 4) Train segmentation adapters with Focal + Dice on pseudo-masks. 5) Code: make_ot_masks.py; train_zero.py.
EXPERIMENT: BMAD zero-shot leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); no source masks used by the proposed variants; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as reference; 3 seeds; pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Baselines: counterfactual replacement; normal-bank kNN; mask-supervised MVFA. Ablations: number of twins; epsilon and relaxation; levels used. Metrics: pseudo-mask IoU (analysis), held-out pixel AUROC, PRO, image AUROC, preprocessing time. Falsification: IoU not above counterfactual masks.
